descriptionAdvanced.en: The Antofagasta-Bolivia Railway (FCAB) is one of the most iconic and economically significant railway systems in South America. Originally built in the late 19th century, it was designed to transport silver and later tin from the high-altitude mines of Potosí and Oruro to the Pacific port of Antofagasta. The construction of the line was a monumental engineering challenge, as the tracks must climb from sea level to over 4,000 meters in a very short distance. Despite Bolivia losing its coastline in the Pacific War, the railway remains a critical lifeline for the country's landlocked economy, continuing to facilitate the export of vast quantities of zinc and lead. The line passes through some of the most dramatic landscapes on Earth, including the stark Atacama Desert and the volcanic peaks of the Western Cordillera.

en: The railway features one of the world's steepest non-cogwheel gradients on a major freight line.
It was originally built with a narrow gauge of 2 feet 6 inches (762 mm), which was later widened to 1 meter.
The line includes the spectacular Carcote bridge, one of the highest railway bridges in Chile near the Bolivian border.
Today, it primarily serves the San Cristóbal mine and other major mineral projects in the southern Altiplano.
